prerequisites: Basic knowledge of linear algebra and calculus of one real variable.
Fondamenti di informatica course (recommended) in order to be familiar with the main programming constructs.

learning_outcomes.text: Present modern numerical approaches to classical problems in mathematics whose numerical solutions are essential, including linear systems, eigenvalue problems, nonlinear equations, polynomial approximation, and integration.
Explain when and how to use various numerical algorithms, as well as how and why they work.
Analyze the computational facets of the presented methods, like the conditioning of a problem and the stability and complexity of a solution method.
Be introduced to the industry-standard programming environment MATLAB.
Understand the basic concepts behind the various numerical methods studied.
Utilize more sophisticated numerical methods provided as built-in MATLAB functions.
Understand and analyse all computational facets of numerical methods used for solving mathematical problems.
Implement these methods by assessing the quality of numerical results.
Be introduced to the design of composite approaches incorporating tools from computational mathematics and computer science for the solution of applicative problems.

syllabus_topics: Error analysis: roundoff errors and computer arithmetic.
Algorithms: iterative processes, convergence, stability, and complexity.
Review of linear algebra and matrix computations.
Eigenvalues and eigenvectors: orthogonal matrices and similarity transformations.
Matrix factorizations and the Gaussian elimination method.
Iterative methods for linear systems: the general theory of convergence.
The Jacobi and the Gauss-Seidel iterative techniques.
Specialized convergence criteria for diagonally dominant matrices.
Approximating eigenvalues of matrices: The power method and its generalizations.
Algebraic equations: the companion matrix and the eigenvalue connection.
The Lagrange form of the interpolating polynomial.
Composite numerical integration: the composite trapezoidal rule and its convergence.
Over determined linear systems, the least square problem, normal equations, QR factorization
assessment_rules: The exam is focused on computational and implementative issues of numerical methods while part of exam is concerned with the theoretical results around these methods. A final written exam concerning computational and implementative issues of numerical methods is optional at the instructor's discretion. A final oral exam concerns theoretical properties of numerical methods.
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Delle Telecomunicazioni (Telecommunications Engineering), classe L-8 R Ingegneria dell'informazione
